_note: Every number here was measured by this repo's own evaluators on the exact installed file - none is self-reported by the program's author. AHC039 is ranked on the 150-case PRIVATE set, not the 50 public cases: the public score has a +/-40 run-to-run spread on a ~3750 mean, wider than the gap between every candidate we tested. That choice is vindicated by ahc015, where the program with the best public score (gpt56_codex) is REJECTED on the private set - 33/200 cases fail. AHC058 has no private set at all (SimpleTES ships only the 150 public inputs), so its score is IN-SAMPLE: measured on the same inputs the search optimised against. Treat the two numbers differently.

ahc039.approach: Coarse-to-fine grid SA over cell sets. The plane is bucketed into square cells (ladder 2000 -> 1000 -> 500 -> 250 -> 125, each level upsampled 2x from the previous) with weight (#mackerel - #sardine); the search maintains a single connected, simply-connected polyomino with no diagonal pinch, so its boundary always traces exactly one legal rectilinear simple polygon. Every single-cell flip is validated in O(1) by a 256-entry table on the 8-neighbour mask (cyclic run count == 1, plus a 2x2 checkerboard test); weight, perimeter and corner count are maintained incrementally under hard caps of 4e5/cellsize boundary edges and 1000 corners, with an adaptive Lagrange price on perimeter targeting 99.5% of the budget. Level 0 runs 80 independent restarts from weighted-random seed cells and the top 8 states feed a narrowing beam (8 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1) down the ladder. A final exact sub-grid polish moves each polygon edge to the best integer coordinate within +/-61 (= CS/2-1 at CS=125, a bound that makes the move provably collision-free), scoring rectangle deltas exactly from x/y-sorted fish arrays, and a validator mirroring the official tester (bbox-touching self-intersection check, length, vertex count) guards the output with fallback to the unpolished polygon. Measured along the way: a local 50-case replica harness built on the cached public seeds plus the official Rust tester (calibrated against the real harness); a max-flow/min-cut Lagrangian relaxation used purely as a diagnostic, which showed that reassembling the relaxed optimum's components into one connected region (3444 on case 0000) loses to the SA (3628), so I dropped that route; and a 16x-time run plus a best-of-3 variance study which both showed the search is converged (<= +11 left), which is why I stopped tuning. Note on numbers: v8 (identical algorithm, PTG 0.99, env-tunable) measured 3878.96 on 2 repeats while v9 (PTG 0.995, all parameters hardcoded so a stray environment variable cannot perturb the judge run) measured 3872.33 on 3 repeats; the difference is inside the +/-10 run-to-run noise, and I report v9 because it is the file measured last and the hardened build.
ahc039.also_tried: A synthesis pass explored 8 parameter variants on a 200-case local set; its best (mean 3847.0) sat inside the noise band of this program (3839.2) and two variants produced degenerate polygons scoring 1, so nothing replaced it.

ahc039.rank_caveat: rank 1 / 683 is against the IN-CONTEST final standings only - that is the only thing ALE-Bench's rank estimator compares against. It is NOT the all-time record. AtCoder keeps a permanent post-contest leaderboard (https://atcoder.jp/contests/ahc039/standings/extended) where 17+ users have since beaten the contest winner's 566,997. On that board this program's 575,336 would sit 4th.
comparability_warnings: DIFFERENT TEST CASES: ALE-Bench's 150 private cases use its own random 64-bit seeds (7882753771510266308, ...), not AtCoder's hidden 150 contest cases. Same generator and distribution, different draw - so cross-comparison carries sampling error on top of run-to-run variance.

DIFFERENT HARDWARE: measured on an AMD EPYC 9655 (Zen 5, 96C/socket x2). These solutions spend a fixed 1.90s wall-clock budget, so a faster CPU does more annealing iterations and scores higher. AtCoder's judge is slower, so the AtCoder-comparable score is likely BELOW 575,336.
NOT STATISTICALLY RESOLVABLE: the 648-point gap to the all-time #1 (0.113%) is smaller than this program's own run-to-run spread of 838 points (0.146%) on identical cases.
Only an actual AtCoder submission would settle whether this program beats the record.
ahc039.honest_claim: Best program in this repo by a clear margin (+3.52% over the previous best, which is far outside noise), and above the in-contest winner. In the same band as the all-time top submissions, but NOT the record and not demonstrably SOTA.

ahc058.approach:
Core method: represent a plan as an ORDERED PURCHASE SEQUENCE decoded ASAP (buy each item on the first turn it is affordable, idling while saving). This is provably complete — buying earlier never hurts, so any optimal plan is the ASAP decode of some order — and it makes "save up for an expensive machine" a reordering rather than a long chain of idle decisions. Every candidate is scored by an exact __int128 simulation (income tracked incrementally, only ids with a live chain updated per turn), so the objective is the true final apple count, never an estimate. Search = simulated annealing over that sequence (change/insert/erase/move one element, block insert/erase/move, and a chain-id remap that migrates a whole solution from machine id j1 to j2), run as a portfolio: ~50 greedy seeds from a projection-gain greedy over (cost multiplier lambda, optimism q, allowed-chain mask, two-phase money-engine-then-target-chain splits), deduped, then successive halving over 4 phases (14 seeds screened, top third, top sixth, then the leader). A checkpoint ladder (every 32 purchases) means a mutation at index k only re-simulates the suffix, and acceptance rebuilds only from that checkpoint forward — this alone took throughput from 135k to 800k-1.3M evaluated plans per case.

My assigned angle (beam search with a lookahead eval) was implemented three ways and empirically capped out far below the SA, so I adapted: on case 0, a turn-indexed beam with the closed-form "final apples if we stop buying" projection scored 53.9 at width 300 and only 54.17 at width 20000; a time-bucketed beam over macro-actions ("wait until affordable, then buy", which makes saving an explicit fair-comparison branch) scored 53.6; a rollout-evaluated greedy scored 54.0 — versus 57.6 for the exact-eval SA. The reason is structural: a chain purchase (level 2 or 3) only pays off in combination with many later purchases, so any node evaluated by a no-further-purchases projection is dominated by cheap immediate returns regardless of beam width. Exact evaluation of complete plans is what breaks that.

Measurements along the way: the free-money bound (unlimited apples, 500 turns) is log2 = 57.14 + log2(A_max), so money, not turns, is the binding constraint; scaling all costs down confirmed it (case 0: 57.6 at cost x1, 60.1 at x0.3, 63.5 at x1e-6). Convergence checks: 16x more wall time buys only +0.008 combined, and random (non-greedy) starting sequences converge to the same ~57.65 on case 0 — that is why I stopped tuning rather than adding search. Suffix-biased mutation sampling was tried and measurably hurt (1.8879 vs 1.8904), so positions stay uniform; SA temperature, schedule variants, seed count, block size and LNS re-greedy moves were all swept on 150-case 3-repetition local means and were flat or negative. Time limit is 1.85s (measured 1.85s CPU, 0.15s under the strict 2.0s limit); all 3 final harness runs were 150/150 AC.
ahc058.measurement: benchmarks/ale_bench/ahc058/evaluator.py, 150 public inputs x 3 judge runs; 15 judge runs total across 3 sessions
ahc058.note: Four independent agents converged on the same representation - an ordered purchase sequence decoded ASAP, which is provably complete - and all four beat the previous best. Selection between them was by measured head-to-head with non-overlapping min/max bands.
